newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Nov 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Nov 25.

text.p: The following is a summary of major South Korean political stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not gaurantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.

- President Kim Young-sam, attending the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit conference, held a series of meetings with U.S., China and Japan. In the talks, Kim called for North Korea to apologise for a September submarine incursion incident. He also accepted an invitation to visit Japan.

- Korea, U.S., during summit meetings in Manila, separated Seoul's demand for a North Korean apology for a September submarine incursion incident from the long-standing proposal for four-way Korean peninsula peace talks.
- The 45h APEC summit meeting is expected to adopt the Subic manifesto calling for Asia-Pacific trade liberalization by 2010.
- South Korea, reversing its stand, is expected to sign a protocol concluded by the Korean Peninsula Energy Development Organization (KEDO) and North Korea.

- South Korea's Kim Young-sam and U.S. president Bill Clinton discussed North Korea's submarine infiltration during their summit meeting in Manila. Seoul will not link four-way Korean peninsula peace talks to Pyongyong's apology.
- A hijacked Ethiopian jet crashed near the Comoros Islands, killing about 100 passengers, including a 49-year-old South Korean diplomat based in Kenya.
